# Purpose

Award credit for a defensible load path, a correct circular-arc idealization, integration of the varying load per arc length, root equilibrium, local section-resultant resolution, hollow-section properties, combined axial-plus-flexure stress, and a carefully scoped yield assessment.

# Instructor Scope Notes

The supplied diagram is instructor-only. The load intensity is total gravity load per arc length and already includes the calculated baseline steel self-weight. Density and gravity are retained to expose that physical interpretation; changing them changes the inferred exhibit-only share, not the assigned total load intensity.

The baseline ratio $R/H=60$ supports the slender-member straight-beam stress approximation for this classroom check. This is not classical curved-beam neutral-axis theory, a deflection analysis, finite-element analysis, or certification of the complete armature, anchorage, skeleton mount, or exhibit.

The 100 × 50 × 4 mm section is an instructor-assigned teaching geometry and must not be described as a verified stocked commercial product. The 0.93 design-thickness factor and 345 MPa assigned yield strength are consistent with the referenced ASTM A500 teaching convention, but actual material certification and fabricated curved-section properties remain outside scope.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context, function, and load path: 20%;
- student idealization, free-body diagrams, and assumptions: 20%;
- distributed-load equilibrium and section resultants: 30%;
- section properties, combined stress, and factor of safety: 20%;
- engineering assessment and limitations: 10%.
